_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'English Syllabus, Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 11, Topics 11.1-11.5 (structure) / continuing SSEL unit numbering into the low-to-mid teens. Original topic/sub-topic names and Specific Outcome statements as documented in this file's prior version's own notes. Rebuilt 2026-08-31 to add real term/week/content data from a second real source, a complete 'SCHEME OF WORK' covering all 3 grades × all 3 terms, organized week-by-week and lesson-by-lesson (not by skill-strand block like the CDC syllabus's own structure) — the user explicitly chose a full rebuild around this source's real teaching units rather than a lighter overlay onto the old skill-strand topics, given how differently the two are organized. Real PII stripped, per standing sourcing policy: every term header in the source repeated a real individual's full name; removed and does not appear anywhere in this file. The source's own publisher/repackager branding (a materials-vendor name, not an individual's real school) was also removed from every header, out of caution. Topics here are the real 'Unit' themes this source actually teaches (e.g. 'Unit 1: Teachers and Teaching'), each containing the real individual lessons (Reading, Composition, Structure, Oral, Summary — genuinely interleaved within a unit in the real record, not grouped by strand); weeks with no named unit (mostly term-opening orientation weeks) are grouped under 'General Language Skills'. Each sub-topic's week_number is the real week it was first taught; where the source's own table cell for a lesson was just 'As above' (repeating the prior lesson's content across a second/third period in the same week), only the first occurrence is kept rather than duplicated. Content was extracted programmatically from the source's raw table (thousands of individual cells across 9 grade/term blocks) rather than transcribed by hand, then spot-checked for parsing errors before being written here; a handful of rows whose table formatting was too garbled to confidently attribute were left out rather than guessed. Real irregularity found and documented, not silently fixed or deduplicated: this source's Grade 11 Term 1 and Term 2 sections are a near-verbatim duplicate of each other — direct comparison found 24 of 28 real lesson entries identical, including matching real week numbers, with only trivial wording differences in the remainder (e.g. 'Composition' vs 'Comprehension' in one label). This is almost certainly a template copy-paste error in the source document itself. Both terms are reproduced faithfully as found in the source, exactly as extracted, rather than fabricating distinct content for one of them or silently removing the apparent duplicate.
